problem: VLN training data is limited in scale and diversity because it comes from manually curated simulators. Prior web-video approaches (AirBERT, YTB-VLN) use template instructions or discrete panoramas and ignore object variety and 3D path geometry.
motivation: Room tour videos are abundant and capture continuous human walking through real homes with rich objects and layouts. With 3D reconstruction and expert vision models, they can supply geometry-aware, open-vocabulary navigation data at scale, which a generalist LLM-based agent can use to generalize better.
key_idea: Turn YouTube room tour videos into geometry-aware VLN data (COLMAP trajectories, object/depth/room annotations, GPT-4 instructions, navigable-action candidates) and use it to train NaviLLM.
insight: Richer grounded context in the generated descriptions helps: in the ablation on input modalities, adding object tags, depth plus bounding boxes, and room type raises R2R SPL from 56.67 to 62.28 and REVERIE SPL from 31.35 to 37.10. Action-enriched trajectories with reconstructed geometry teach action selection from frames without panoramas. Without any action data NaviLLM gets 0 SR in the zero-shot setting, and adding RoomTour3D actions gives 14.33 SR.
method: Video collection: 1847 YouTube room tour videos (243 h), filtered with GPT-4 on titles and descriptions, minimum 3 min, few shot changes; downsampled to 3 fps at shorter side 360.

Description-enriched trajectories: frames sampled every 2 s; RAM tags, Grounding-DINO boxes and Depth-Anything depth are textualized as left/middle/right and near/closer/far; BLIP-2 predicts room type (16 classes, temporally smoothed); GPT-4-Turbo generates trajectory descriptions (~100K trajectories, ~200K instructions).
3D reconstruction: COLMAP on 100 s clips with 10 s overlap; sub-models merged by DFS over an overlap graph (>3 shared frames), with rollback if reprojection error increases.

Navigable action sampling: view-change points (>45° via cosine similarity), non-maximum suppression, DBSCAN clustering; per walking path, the latest frame is the positive candidate and the frame with the highest angular difference is the negative (~17K action-enriched trajectories).
Summarization pretraining task: frames are treated as <cand> views and NaviLLM is trained with next-token loss to summarize object progression and room locations.
Navigation finetuning task: each frame is a step; the model selects the next frame from candidates or STOP, with a final trajectory summarization step.
Training setup: NaviLLM (Vicuna-7B, EVA-CLIP frozen) is pretrained and then multi-task finetuned with RoomTour3D added to CVDN, SOON, R2R, REVERIE, ScanQA and LLaVA-23k.

setting.backbone: NaviLLM (Vicuna-7B-v1.1 + 2-layer multi-view fusion transformer, EVA-CLIP-02-Large frozen), fine-tuned
setting.training_data: RoomTour3D (~100K description-enriched trajectories / ~200K instructions, 17K action-enriched trajectories, 1847 videos) plus CVDN, SOON, R2R, REVERIE, ScanQA, augmented R2R/REVERIE, LLaVA-23k
setting.observation: panoramic RGB views for the benchmarks; monocular video frames as candidate views for RoomTour3D
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoint selection among candidate views (frames for RoomTour3D data), plus STOP
setting.privileged: none (REVERIE uses the standard GT object boxes at waypoints)

numbers.method: NaviLLM+RT3D (zero-shot, no action/geometry data in base training)
numbers.extra: all action and geometric data removed from base training; only RT3D action-enriched trajectories give navigation ability

numbers_note: Table 1 SPL values for SOON, R2R and REVERIE are stated in the caption; R2R and REVERIE cells appear to be SPL. SR values for the supervised main rows are not printed in Table 1. Table 2 gives SR/SPL on val-unseen for the description-enriched ablation.
results: Adding RoomTour3D to NaviLLM improves CVDN, SOON, R2R and REVERIE. For example, R2R val-unseen SPL goes from 56.7 (reproduced) to 62.4 and REVERIE from 31.4 to 37.4. It sets state-of-the-art results on SOON and REVERIE, with SOON SPL 31.7 on val-unseen. In the zero-shot setting it reaches 14.33 SR, above NavCoT (7.78) and comparable to NavGPT with GPT-3.5, but below GPT-4 based methods.
limitations: Zero-shot performance (14.33 SR) is far below GPT-4/GPT-4V-based zero-shot agents (34-43.7 SR).
Data quality depends on noisy automatic tools: COLMAP reconstruction, BLIP-2 room labels at 85% accuracy, and GPT-generated descriptions with a 3.08/4 average rating.
Training is expensive (32 A100 for pretraining) and the study is on one backbone (NaviLLM) in simulated indoor benchmarks only.
